 Home Business News Financial Rules Changing From November 2026: From ITR Deadlines And Pensions To GST, Know 5 Key Changes
 November 2026 brings significant financial updates, including extended ITR deadlines, revised GST provisions, and potential LPG price changes. Pensioners must submit life certificates, while PNB credit card users face new service charges and late fees. By Chetna Shree 
 Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:09 PM (IST) 
 Source: JND 
 5 Key Financial Rules Changing From November 2026. (Representational Image/Canva Related Articles HighLights Pensioners must submit annual life certificates by November 30.
 ITR filing deadline extended for audited taxpayers until November 21.
 Revised GST provisions, LPG prices, and PNB credit card fees.
 November 2026 brings a fresh set of financial deadlines, tax updates, and banking fees revisions that could directly impact monthly household budgets and routine financial transactions. Key updates include annual life certificate submissions for pensioners, extended income tax return (ITR) deadlines, revised Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) provisions, monthly LPG price adjustments, and revised credit card charges for Punjab National Bank (PNB) customers.
 ALSO READ:  LPG Cylinder New Rules From Nov 1: Revision In Prices To Booking Rules, Check Key Changes; Will It Affect Your Kitchen Budget? 
 Annual Life Certificate Submission For Pensioners
 Government pensioners under 80 years of age can submit their annual life certificates between November 1 and November 30 to ensure uninterrupted monthly pension payouts. Pensioners aged 80 and above have been eligible to complete this process since October 1.
 Additionally, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) has introduced the UPS Jeevan Setu Digital Life Certificate (DLC) facility for Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) subscribers, who can submit their certificates online using the Protean eGov App by November 30, NDTV reported.

 Extended ITR Filing Deadline For Audited Taxpayers
 Eligible taxpayers whose accounts require an audit have received extra time to complete their filings for FY 2025-26. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) extended the Income Tax Return (ITR) filing deadline from October 31 to November 21, 2026. This relief applies specifically to eligible businesses, firms, and professionals who submitted their tax audit reports by the October 21 deadline.
 Revised GST Provisions From November 1
 Amendments to certain provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017, will come into effect on November 1, 2026. The changes cover post-supply discounts, credit notes, and GST refunds.
 Under the updated guidelines, businesses must comply with revised conditions, including reversing input tax credits (ITC) linked to post-sale discounts, to exclude them from taxable supply values. Adjustments to GST refund processes for inverted duty structures will also take effect.

 Changes In LPG Cylinder Rates
 The Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) will review Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) rates on November 1, 2026. Accordingly, rates for both 14.2 kg domestic cylinders and 19 kg commercial cylinders could be revised.
 A change in domestic LPG prices will directly impact household kitchen budgets, while revisions in commercial cylinder rates will impact restaurants, hotels, and other businesses that rely on cooking gas.
 PNB Revises Credit Card Charges And Late Fees
 Punjab National Bank (PNB) cardholders using Visa and RuPay credit cards will see revised service charges starting November 1, 2026:
 ATM Cash Withdrawals: Cash withdrawals at PNB ATMs will incur a revised fee of 2.5 per cent of the transaction amount or Rs 400, whichever is higher. Cash withdrawals at non-PNB domestic ATMs will incur a fee of 2.5 per cent or Rs 500, whichever is higher.
 Late Payment Charges: Outstanding dues up to Rs 500 will incur no late fee. However, late charges for higher outstanding dues have been revised, capped at a maximum fee of Rs 1,200 for dues exceeding Rs 50,000.
 Utility Payments Charges: Cardholders making utility bill payments exceeding Rs 50,000 in a billing cycle will see a 1 per cent processing fee, capped at Rs 2,000 per transaction.
 Additional Updates: Revisions have been made to cheque returns, auto-debit dishonour fees, and reward point redemptions.
